title: New User, Zero History
instruction: A brand-new visitor just arrived with no history. Does this strategy work for them today?

items.why: Popularity needs data about everyone, not about this user: a safe default.

items.text: Use the visitor's country, language and device
items.why: Context is available from the very first request.

items.text: Ask them to pick three favourite genres
items.why: A short onboarding question gives a few explicit preferences immediately.

items.text: Use the first three clicks of this visit
items.why: Session-based recommendation works without any account history.

items.text: Show editors' picks and curated lists
items.why: Hand-picked lists need no data about the visitor at all.

items.text: Find taste twins from their rating history
items.why: User-to-user collaborative filtering needs ratings this visitor doesn't have yet.

items.text: Factorize their rating history into taste factors
items.why: Matrix factorization needs a row of interactions to learn this user's factors.

items.text: Predict preferences from their watch history
items.why: Same problem: no history, nothing to predict from.

debrief: For a new user, start with what needs no history (popularity, context, a few onboarding answers, the clicks of this session) and hand over to personalization as history builds up.
